lead: All the shellfish peeled. No shells, no mess. The rice where comfort is the luxury: clean prawns, squid, cuttlefish and monkfish, over a rockfish fumet and Alicante-style salmorreta.

Arroz del senyoret is the most “no excuses” rice in Valencian cooking. There are no shells to separate, no bones to pick out, no hands to wash. All the shellfish arrives already peeled and cleaned, built straight into the grain of rice. It is the rice you can eat looking out to sea with a glass of white wine in your hand, without interruption.

Its popularity along the whole Valencian and Alicante coast is enormous. It appears on almost every beach restaurant menu, in the rice restaurants of central Valencia and on the tables of the restaurants of Jávea, Altea and Dénia. It is the most welcoming rice for diners with no experience of seafood rices: the flavour is just as powerful, but the experience far more comfortable.

items.title: Arròs del Senyoret · The Young Gentleman’s Rice
items.subtitle: All the shellfish peeled · No messy hands · The luxury of eating in comfort
items.body: Arroz del senyoret — literally “the young gentleman’s” — is one of the most elegant and comfortable rices in Valencian cooking. Its hallmark is as simple as it is irresistible: all the shellfish and fish reaches the plate already peeled, cleaned and ready, with no shells, no bones, no work. Peeled prawns, chopped squid, clean cuttlefish, boneless monkfish, shelled mussels. The diner needs only a spoon. It is a dry rice in the paella style, cooked in the same pan and with the same technique, but where comfort is the luxury. The seafood fumet — made with the heads and shells of the shellfish itself — concentrates all the flavour of the Mediterranean, and the Alicante salmorreta — garlic, ñora pepper, tomato and parsley — adds the touch of aromatic depth that sets this rice apart from any other seafood dish.
facts: Dry rice, paella style · Everything peeled and cleaned · Homemade seafood fumet · Optional Alicante salmorreta

items.title: The Origin · The Young Gentleman of the Malvarrosa
items.subtitle: Around 1950 · Malvarrosa beach · Joaquín Sorolla · The wealthy houses of Alicante
items.body: The origin of arroz del senyoret has two equally possible versions. The most popular says that, around 1950, a young man from a good family known as “the Senyoret” frequented a restaurant on the Malvarrosa beach in Valencia and always ordered rice with seafood without shell or bones. The cooks adapted the recipe to his taste and named it after his nickname. The second version points to the Valencian painter Joaquín Sorolla, closely linked to Jávea: according to this story, Sorolla once asked in a rice restaurant for the langoustines to be peeled and placed on top of the rice. The cooks went a step further and peeled all the shellfish directly. There is also a third, older version: the dish was prepared in the wealthy houses of Alicante and the servants presented the rice with all the ingredients peeled so that the young master of the house would not have to dirty his hands or put down his spoon at any moment.
facts: Version 1: The Senyoret of the Malvarrosa, c. 1950 · Version 2: Joaquín Sorolla in Jávea · Version 3: wealthy houses of Alicante

items.title: The Salmorreta · The Alicante Secret
items.subtitle: Dried ñora · Garlic · Tomato · Parsley · The aromatic base of Alicante rices
items.body: The ingredient that sets arroz del senyoret apart from other seafood paellas is the salmorreta: a thick, dark paste made by frying dried ñoras — a type of small, round, dried pepper — with garlic, grated tomato and parsley, and then blending everything into a concentrated pâté. This sauce is the aromatic base of the great Alicante rices — arroz a banda, arroz del senyoret, rice with prawns and salmorreta — and gives the broth a unique depth and colour. The ñora, in particular, contributes a slightly sweet, smoky flavour for which there is no substitute. The salmorreta is added to the paella together with the cuttlefish and the squid before the fumet goes in, and at that moment it permeates all the oil and ingredients with its characteristic aroma.
facts: Salmorreta: dried ñora + garlic + grated tomato + parsley · Fry in oil · Blend in a mortar · Typical of Alicante rices

items.title: Senyoret vs Arroz a Banda · The Differences
items.subtitle: Often confused · Arroz a banda has no chunks · The senyoret does · Two different dishes
items.body: Arroz del senyoret and arroz a banda are frequently confused, but they are different though related dishes. Arroz a banda was originally a seafarers’ dish from fishing boats: it was served in two stages — first the fish and vegetables cooked in the broth, and then the rice cooked in that broth “a banda” (aside, in Valencian) —, with no chunks. Just rice, concentrated rockfish fumet and alioli. The senyoret, by contrast, is a rice with chunks: prawns, squid, cuttlefish and fish, peeled and cleaned, which are integrated into the rice during cooking. The key to the senyoret is that those chunks have no shell or bone. Nowadays many restaurants give both dishes the same name, which has created some confusion. The real difference: if it has peeled chunks, it is senyoret; if it is just rice with broth and nothing else, it is a banda.
facts: Arroz a banda: no chunks, just rice and fumet · Senyoret: with shellfish and fish, peeled, integrated into the rice

items.title: The Fumet · The Key to the Rice
items.subtitle: Rockfish broth and shellfish heads · The canvas of flavour · Always hot
items.body: As in all the great Valencian seafood rices, the key to the senyoret lies in the fumet. The senyoret fumet is made with the heads and shells of the prawns, monkfish bones or other white fish, mantis shrimp, crabs and morralla (small rockfish). Everything is first fried in oil, a little tomato, onion and leek are added, water is poured over and it is left to simmer gently for 20 to 30 minutes. The result is a dark, briny, concentrated broth full of marine flavour. The key: the fumet must be hot when it is added to the rice — cold broth breaks the cooking. The usual proportion is 2.5 parts fumet to 1 of rice. When it is added, the saffron and the toasted saffron go in too. The fumet left over from peeling the shellfish for the senyoret is exactly the best fumet possible: nothing is wasted.
facts: Fumet: prawn heads + morralla + mantis shrimp · Cooking 20–30 min · Always hot · Proportion: 2.5 parts fumet : 1 rice

items.title: The heads are the broth
items.body: Never throw away the prawn heads — they are the base of the tastiest fumet possible

items.title: Salmorreta before the fumet
items.body: Add the salmorreta with the cuttlefish and the squid — let it soak in well before the broth

items.title: Fumet always hot
items.body: Cold broth breaks the rice’s cooking — keep it boiling before adding

items.title: Prawns at the end
items.body: Add the peeled prawns for the last 5 minutes — if cooked too long they turn rubbery

items.title: Don’t stir the rice
items.body: As in any paella, once the fumet is added the rice is not stirred

items.title: Rest under a cloth
items.body: 5 min covered with a cloth after turning off the heat — the rice finishes absorbing the broth

items.title: Malvarrosa Beach
items.body: The cradle of the myth. The restaurants on the seafront promenades of the Malvarrosa and the Cabanyal serve arroz del senyoret in its original context: facing the sea, with a Mediterranean breeze.

items.title: Central Valencia
items.body: Several rice restaurants in the historic centre and the Eixample prepare signature versions of the senyoret with red prawn, peeled langoustine or lobster. The Mercado Central and its surroundings are the epicentre.

items.title: Alicante coast · Jávea · Altea
items.body: The territory most closely tied to the senyoret. The restaurants of the north coast of Alicante have it as their star dish. In Jávea, the connection with Sorolla and the seafaring tradition makes the experience the most authentic.

items.title: Signature restaurants in Valencia
items.body: The chefs of Valencia’s leading restaurants make versions of the senyoret with seasonal ingredients from the fish market: mantis shrimp, wedge clams, red king prawn and the catch of the day.

blocks.title: What you should know about arroz del senyoret
items: The senyoret is not the same as arroz a banda — a banda has no chunks; the senyoret does, but all peeled
Salmorreta (ñora, garlic, tomato, parsley) is the distinguishing ingredient — without it, it is simply a seafood paella
The best senyoret fumet is made with the heads and shells of the very shellfish that goes on the plate — nothing is wasted
The peeled prawns go in at the end — the last 5 minutes of cooking, or they will turn rubbery
Arroz del senyoret allows peeled lobster as a luxury version — in that case it is called “senyoret de bogavante”
It is served with alioli on the side for whoever wants to add it — it pairs perfectly with the marine flavour of the fumet and the salmorreta
